key_insight: Citizen-led PV remains viable under declining electricity prices mainly when users coordinate self-consumption and sharing strategies, not when relying on oversized generation or storage.
engineering_relevance: For distributed energy system design, the paper shows that governance and allocation rules can matter as much as hardware choices in maximizing local use, savings, and project sustainability.
method: Analyzed high-resolution consumption data from a rural community with 24 users sharing one PV facility
Compared static, dynamic, and hybrid energy-sharing models
Evaluated configurations with and without battery storage under current market and remuneration conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that collective self-consumption lowers required PV capacity and investment cost while increasing annual savings versus individually operated systems, with storage adding limited value in most current-price scenarios.
watch_item: Benefits depend on trade-offs between efficiency, fairness, and governance complexity, so implementation may be harder than the technical optimization suggests.
paper_title: Decision-support strategies for photovoltaic self-consumption under declining electricity prices and limited remuneration of surplus generation
